note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is, and 'endorsements' is empty for a reason: no Nebraska party page that a program may read says it endorses a candidate for a November 3, 2026 state or local race. What the parties publish instead are lists of their own candidates, and in Nebraska those lists say more than the ballot does, because the Legislature, the State Board of Education, the Regents, and every city, school and district board are printed without a party. Each record under other_support is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only), with the page's own word in 'kind': the Nebraska Democratic Party calls its list 'the 300+ candidates we are supporting this cycle' and marks the six who are not Democrats '(Independent)'; the Nebraska Republican Party, the Douglas County Democratic Party and the Douglas County Republican Party publish bare lists of their candidates (the last as a card shown as a picture, read by eye and checked by its SHA-256, b80cafdcf534826c003efd0db899557a9fa39aa313f0dd4c24b2e7e3eef358b7). None of them is an endorsement and none may be shown as one. The same candidate often stands on a state list and a county list: count a candidate once per party. A line on a partisan office (Governor, county offices) adds nothing to the party label on the ballot and is kept only so that each list is whole. Four lines were matched although the page spells the name differently from the ballot, by one letter or by the order of a two-part family name (Raislback for Railsback, Piedrahitra for Piedrahita, Theresa for Teresa Ibach, Janelle Ehrke-Anderson for Janell Anderson Ehrke); 'as_listed' keeps the page's spelling. A Governor's and a Lieutenant Governor's lines are one record, as they are one choice on the ballot. Lines under other_support_unmatched_listed could not be tied to a race: for nearly all of them the county's village, township or school contests are not loaded yet. Federal offices are outside this file. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first; every page in 'lists' was opened a second time and parsed again, and a record is kept only if both readings show it (none was lost). Facebook pages, which are all most county units have, are social media and were not read.
